_comment: MEASURED roofline-vs-measured for DeepSeek-V4-Flash's DOMINANT op -- the routed-expert MoE grouped-GEMM (68% of decode) -- on EMR (uPP stream_triad: 226 GB/s per NUMA domain). Experts are native MXFP4 W4A16 (compute-from-native-precision: packed fp4 nibbles fed straight to the AMX kernel, fused fp4->bf16, no dequant footprint blowup). Roofline = per-domain DRAM bandwidth; measured = achieved streaming bandwidth at three operating points (bench_mxfp4_moe_roofline.py, this session). Story: prefill and BATCHED decode run near the memory roofline (~75%); UNBATCHED M=1 decode is bandwidth-starved (~26%) -> continuous batching is the decode lever. Model-level measured (EMR, tp=1 + decode-cap=8, full 43 layers, batch 32): prefill 69.6 / decode 9.3 tok/s. Forward target not yet run: GNR fp8 batch-32 decode 146.7 tok/s (higher BW + fp8).
model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash — routed-expert MoE kernel (68% of decode)
node: EMR Xeon (1 NUMA domain; uPP stream_triad 226 GB/s)

ops.note: near the memory roofline; native MXFP4 fed straight to the AMX kernel (no dequant blowup)
continuous batching amortizes weight streaming -> recovers BW (the decode lever)
bandwidth-starved at M=1; fixed by batching, not by a new kernel
